ig_carousel_topic.topic: Hedging, when it's smart, when it's just buying back losses
ig_carousel_topic.slide1_text: Hedging: Smart Risk Management or Scared Money?
ig_carousel_topic.slide2_text: Most bettors hedge because they're nervous, not because the math works. You placed a +250 futures bet. It's alive. Now you want to lay the other side to 'guarantee' a profit. That feeling is almost never the right signal.
ig_carousel_topic.slide3_text: A hedge makes sense when the expected value of locking in a profit NOW beats the expected value of riding it out. That means the implied probability has shifted so far in your favor that the juice on the hedge is worth paying. That is rare. Most hedges cost you more than they protect.
ig_carousel_topic.slide4_text: Example: You bet Team A to win the title at +400 for 1 unit. They reach the final. The other side is now -180. Hedging costs 1.8 units to guarantee roughly 0.9u profit. Riding it out: if Team A wins you net +4u. If they lose, -1u. EV of riding it out is higher unless you genuinely need the cash now.
ig_carousel_topic.slide5_text: Hedge when the math says to, not when your stomach says to. Run the numbers before you place the back-bet. If the hedge costs more than half your potential profit, you're buying back anxiety, not managing risk.
ig_carousel_topic.caption: Hedging feels smart. The math usually disagrees. Swipe through before your next futures bet tempts you to cover.
